functions.description: Convert a container volume given with its unit to cubic metres
inputs: the volume of the container holding the gas with unit

functions.description: Convert a temperature given with its unit to kelvin.
inputs: the temperature of the gas with unit

functions.description: Compute the pressure of a perfect gas from its amount, absolute temperature and volume using p = nRT/V
Check that a predicted perfect gas pressure is insensitive to rounding the temperature to 300 K.
outputs: pressure agrees at the rounded temperature to the stated significant figures

functions.description: Express a pressure given in pascals in megapascals, bar and atmospheres for reference.
Round a computed value to a stated number of significant figures and attach its unit.
inputs: number of significant figures to report

functions.description: Predict the pressure exerted by a confined perfect gas from its amount, temperature and container volume using the perfect gas equation.
inputs: the amount of substance of the gas with unit (number of moles n)
the chemical formula of the gas with its physical state label
the volume of the container holding the gas with unit
the temperature of the gas with unit
the common name of the gas species
outputs: predicted pressure of the gas with unit

entry_points.text: Suppose that ●1 ●2 is confined to ●3 at ●4. Predict the pressure exerted by the ●5 from the perfect gas equation.

params.description: the amount of substance of the gas with unit (number of moles n)
params.validity_range: Must be a finite positive number of moles; zero or negative amounts are physically meaningless for a confined gas, and very large amounts are valid only as far as the perfect gas model holds.

params.description: the chemical formula of the gas with its physical state label
params.validity_range: Must be a gas-phase species at the stated conditions so that the perfect gas equation applies; condensed or liquid species are not covered by this model.

params.description: the volume of the container holding the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a finite positive volume; the result is inversely proportional to volume and diverges as the volume approaches zero, so the perfect gas model is valid only for volumes not so small that molecular volume matters.

params.description: the temperature of the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Must be above absolute zero, i.e. greater than -273.15°C or greater than 0 K, and the gas must remain in the gas phase at that temperature; the perfect gas model is least accurate at low temperatures and high pressures.

params.description: the common name of the gas species
params.validity_range: Must name the same substance as the chemical formula given for the amount; it is used only for narration and identification and does not change the calculation.
